node: Indonesia nickel export routing, resource nationalism, and HPAL supply-chain exposure
summary: Layer 1B expansion found a two-lane universe for the Indonesia nickel export-control node. The reference lane is Vale because it has direct Indonesia nickel exposure and can anchor what the market already recognizes. The underfollowed lane is more interesting: Lifezone Metals as a non-Indonesian mine-to-metal nickel alternative, Talon Metals as a speculative North American restart/development alternative with a Tesla offtake, and Ecovyst as an adjacent sulfuric-acid/regeneration name where the connection is indirect but potentially relevant if HPAL acid scarcity becomes a binding chokepoint. Key caveat: the Indonesia centralized export framework and nickel inclusion are still treated as hypothesis from the provided external context; later layers must verify the actual regulation text, commodity scope, contract impact, and whether HPAL acid constraints transmit into listed-company revenue.
